rationale:
The `{cite}` role is right for `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]`.

- **Not an `{impl}` root.** `UsageLog` is only reached from items already marked `{impl}` for `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`. These are `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_output]` and `PendingAssessment`'s `persisted` and `failed`. The record fields (version, run, root, subject, times, outcome, determination, evidence output and written) live in `UsageRecord`, which `UsageLog` only holds. `start` creates the per-run file `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` and `save` writes it, so `UsageLog` is not the place where the requirement is decided.
- **Not a `{test}`.** It is a data type, not a test.
- **A `{cite}` is justified.** The struct pairs a `record: UsageRecord` with a `path: PathBuf`. That models the requirement's "separate JSON usage record" per assessment, persisted for later review. A change to that text could require changing the struct. One example is a shared record instead of a per-run file, or a record that exists only in memory in stdout mode.
- **Not redundant.** The struct has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement.

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
